tips.comment: Miss Goldfire and her seven-pound claiming apprentice rider are on a hat-trick bid after two comfortable wins in over hurdles. The latest was a conditional jockeys' handicap hurdle over course and distance. This time, she has the Skeltons to beat in the form of Deep Purple.
Finished fourth, beaten by 3 lengths, in a 2m5f handicap hurdle at Warwick last time out. That form holds up well. Showing steady progress.

Produced a decent debut at Fontwell, keeping a listed bumper contender honest on their hurdle debut and entitled to come on for that. Running speed in that race was a km per hour quicker than the other two contenders have managed in their most competitive races. Whilst the effect of this morning's rain on the ground is unknown, it is for all of these who have enjoyed their best days on quick ground. Is value at 5s.

Salley Gardens has benefitted from the switch back to fences after several unsuccessful runs over hurdles. He has won his last two handicap chases under Sean Bowen including over course and distance last time and should get the hat trick.

Unlucky to be done by a subsequent winner over 2m at Taunton and I can forgive the latest run when making a bad blunder early on. I don't think this race will take much winning and it is simply too big a price.

Interesting to see him back under rules from a mark 10lb lower than when he was with Paul Nicholls. He has run well enough in points since to think that at least some ability remains and he has finished first and third on his two visits to this track.

The model I run suggests Do Your Job can win this one. Do Your Job lines up here with the highest RPR for the field and an official ranking closer to the middle of the order. This leaves Do Your Job with less weight to carry around this 2m 4f trip. Again, big odds of 17s, which offers good value relative to the win probability the model suggests. Comes here with reasonable form figures of 5134-4. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Pounding Poet won twice in both 2021 and 2022 but has not won since. He looked unlucky last time when not beaten far at Ayr and not getting a clear run. He is up two pounds for his latest run but is actually still twelve pounds below his last winning mark.

The model I run suggests Party Business can win this one. Party Business lines up here with the highest RPR by quite some way. The official rating is the lowest, which subsequently means he carries the least initial amount of weight. Party Business comes here after a 4th placed finish 30 days ago, so race fitness should be fine. 5s looks like reasonable value, and for that reason, the model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator. This is a 1pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

I really don’t think you will see a better stable debutant. We’ve already seen Hughie Morrison improve Eyed 25lb from the same yard and I think this six-year-old showed more form for his previous handler. It was smashed up last week, but pulled out because the ground was too quick. Sean Bowen is now on board, so you know it's down to try.
Really have to take an interest in this horse when back at Uttoxeter. Cracking record here, more so with the visor. That is now back on and Hughes is booked to ride. I will be dutching.

Russian Virtue, after a couple of healthy spins on the flat, returns to hurdles dropped to Class 5 after being consistent in three previous Class 4 runs. Down 2lb lower than the last winning mark, and the rider claims another 7lb. Yard in form, and he may not need a personal best to win this.

Lily Pinchin has won twice at Huntingdon on Ikigai Star, last time making all unchallenged over a similar distance to this race at Uttoxeter. He is only up three pounds as he may not have beaten much in a 4-horse race, but they could follow up here.

Is a course winner over 2 miles here at Uttoxeter on Good to Soft ground. Drops 2lb for his latest effort at Worcester 30 days ago. The track should suit better here as the horse is proven over it, and if seeing out the extra 4f, he would have an each-way chance. Trainer's only horse of the day.
Disappointed, finishing well back in a Cheltenham handicap hurdle last time. Was in solid form before that. First time tongue tie applied. Dropping in grade is a positive.

The model I run suggests the value option here is Clondaw Royale. Clondaw Royale lines up here with the highest RPR of the entire field and has an official ranking closer towards the middle of the order. This leaves Clondaw Royale carrying less weight than suggested potential. 21s is a massive price and clearly not favoured by the early market. Last ran 15 days ago and came 7th but needed the run after a break. Race fitness now topped up and has the opportunity in this race. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Bluebella can win this one. Bluebella lines up here with the highest RPR of the field, but the lowest official ranking. This leaves Bluebella going around this 2m trip with the lowest weight to carry. Bluebella is a prior distance winner and was unfortunate to unseat the rider 14 days ago. Can get back into the groove here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run indicates Harry's Hope can win this one. Harry's Hope lines up here with a very comparable RPR but an official ranking that leaves him well treated off this mark. Goes out carrying an initial weight that is 11 lbs less than the current market favorite. 112P-2 form figures and last ran 31 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. Looks to go one better here off this 5 horse race. Model issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Blue Nguru finished 3rd on debut behind impressive winner Indigo Dawn at Goodwood last month. He looks sure to improve from that and looks the most likely winner here.

This should lie between Blue Nguru and Midnight Tango, who both showed good pace in decent races at Goodwood and Newmarket, respectively. Both lost places late on, with Midnight Tango leading until 2f out but dropping to 4th eventually, while Blue Nguru challenged for the lead a furlong out but dropped to 3rd. Midnight Tango looks better value if she lasts the 6f at Hamilton.

The two most backed horses here will probably be the pair that have journeyed up from Berkshire hoping to find easier pickings in Scotland. Think they can be taken on with a well bred newcomer, the Kodiac filly, Impalaka, who should offer a value price. The grand sire, Monsieur Bond, ticks boxes for going on the soft side of good and there is a bit of rain around at present so the surface may have some give.

Heavily supported in the market last time at Ayr when sent off 6/5 favourite but only put into contention in the closing stages and far too late, finishing a disappointing 3rd. Makes a rare move away from Ayr and Musselburgh. Trainer Jim Goldie has a good record at Hamilton with a 16% strike rate this season.

Horse number 3 is the current favourite but i can't quite see why myself, that one will need improvement. This selection was well backed when winning last time out in what was a half decent race, this race doesn't look much tougher , connections have possibly found a good opportunity for this horse. Trip and ground conditions ideal, can get competitive from this rating.

The 4yo is suited by this undulating track. Two return runs, not suited by the quick ground last time out, but ran a decent return and fitness should be fine. The returning jockey was in the saddle for back-to-back wins over this 5f C/D last Sept - high RPR ratings. Weighted to be in the mix.

A fast filly who was left behind last time when the break for the front came. She still finished strongly; however, she missed her chance by being too far back. Gets a chance to go again over course and distance and should do better from a good draw in stall 3.
Willingly is well-weighted on prior 5f sprint form and is hitting form, finishing runner-up last week at Chepstow, only beaten a neck. Compensation awaits today.

After a win and two 2nd places, Sir Garfield is due to go up a further two pounds in the handicap and should confirm Ayr form with several rivals who finished behind him. Stall 1 should not be an inconvenience as most of his main rivals are drawn low.

This former course and distance winner missed the break and was slow away over 7 furlongs at Ayr 15 days ago but finished well and beaten 3 lengths. Will need to break smarter and if she does she should go close.
Jump the Gun is now over twenty pounds below his last winning mark and showed he was returning to form last time at Ayr under this jockey and a similar effort should make him competitive here.

This mare is a real C&D specialist, having won 6 times from 22 attempts. So effectively, we're getting 12/1 about a horse that wins more than 1 in 4 races over C&D. Five of the 6 wins were for today's jockey, and they were all off marks in the 60s, whilst the horse races off just 59 here. She had 2 unplaced runs elsewhere to start her campaign last year before winning here, and it could well be a similar story this year too.

Two runs for the 4yo filly this year, only beaten a length two weeks ago and can take a step forward. She travelled nicely, didn’t have a lot of room on the rail, slightly hampered a furlong out but hit the line strongly. Every chance at this level.

Belsito looks interesting in this Hamilton handicap. Rain is forecast, and with 'soft' in the going description for both his wins, conditions could come right for him. His last win was on soft ground at Carlisle last June, and he was also second on soft at Redcar late last year. Unplaced at Haydock on his return from a break, he was 4th of 8 back at Carlisle last week. Only 2 lbs higher than his last win, he looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer if the going deteriorates.
Won off 62 LTO, up to 67 now, handles the cut. Yard are really flying at the moment. Well handicapped based on past class. Top jockey on board in Connor Beasley.

this seven-year-old gelding has demonstrated consistent form that suggests he could be competitive here. In his most recent outing on 24 May 2025 at Catterick, Ramon Di Loria finished fourth in a Class 5 handicap over 5 furlongs and 212 yards, beaten by 2 lengths. Prior to that, he was seventh at Musselburgh on 2 May 2025 over 7 furlongs and 15 yards, indicating a need to recapture his earlier form. Notably, he secured a victory at Ayr on 28 April 2025 in a Class 6 handicap over 6 furlongs, showcasing his potential when conditions suit. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level.

DWINDLING FUNDS is interesting because ace experienced jockey Paul Mulrennan chooses to ride. Scottish trainer Jim Goldie fields others in this handicap . so this four year old potential improver would at the very least be worth a market check come post time.
Hasn't won for a while, but this could be the day. Is on a nice handicap mark and ran well in a hot race last time, coming 3rd at York.

Connections were hoping for better things for the 4yo filly last year after earning a nice 92 rating as a 2yo. However, she returned from a 7 month break with a nice 2L+ win three weeks ago over this 6f trip. Plenty to like how she sprinted through the line despite having a poor track position. Higher mark for this handicap but she can progress.

Korker can be opposed here given his poor FlatStats rating and K Burke’s 21% SR (A/E 0.47) with favourites over 6f at Hamilton. Tropical Island can too be ruled out given his equally as poor FS rating plus the R Fahey yard form (2/47, A/E 0.3 over the past fortnight) and O Orr’s 6% SR (A/E 0.4) on Thursdays. Next up VANTHEMAN makes plenty of appeal however, now down to his last winning mark and back up to 6f. You can forgive him for his below-par effort at York LTO; he was slowly away over 5f and that’s usually all she wrote in that scenario, and I’m not convinced he took to Newmarket’s undulations on seasonal appearance in April. This is much calmer waters for the son of Invincible Army a number of positive stats for the sire boost claims further; most notable being his 38% SR (A/E 1.64) with fancied runners over this trip, 34% SR (A/E 1.4) with fancied runners on straight tracks and impressive 41% SR (A/E 1.81) when you add those two together. 9/2 taken.

Smart Sprinter (despite his age) is coming down to a workable mark. He was a winner the only time that he has run over this C&D in the past, and it was only in the autumn that he wasn't beaten far in much better races from 6 and 7 lb higher than this.

Progressed nicely last term, picking up 3 victories along the way and struck on 2nd start this year when landing a nice race at Pontefract in April. Dropped a lb for what wasn't a bad effort at Newmarket last time and every chance this son of Showcasing could resume his progress this afternoon.
Finished 3 lengths off the pace, running to a mark of 74, over 2m at Chester last time. Thrives when leading. Drops in trip. Proven course winner.

Lightly raced 5yo. Three flat runs this year after joining the good Jim Goldie yard. Only beaten a length in his last two races - good ratings, staying on well and this longer trip could bring about more improvement. Rated much higher last year.

HAPTICS runs with the yard in fine recent form and trainer David O'Meara with jockey Danny Tudhope are 21% when combining at this scottish venue. That reads well for this runner's chance third-up for this spell and given his experienced overall profile when racing in France he could be well placed today.
Likes it around here having won three times before. Still on a handy mark and looks like he is finding some form.
Career best last time out over 2m1f. Strong finisher and will be suited to the drop in trip. Trainer in strong form. Tongue strap is on today, which he's previously won wearing.
Model Approach has had a whisper that the tongue tie has worked wonders and should run a very good race, with a 3lb claimer.

The 4yo has 1 win from 9. Two runs this year, only beaten 1/2L over this 9f C/D three weeks ago, finished strong, good rating posted. Something to build on, room for improvement and the slower ground can help. He was rated quite a bit higher last summer.

Epidavros has not won yet this year but returned in April and did a grand job when second up in a C3 and second off a 74 with PJ in the saddle. While a bit pants here last month, that was on GF. I think the return here today on Good with overnight rain and a 73 could bring her back in.

Pisanello was below par last time at Ripon but normally runs well at Hamilton. Although now an eight-year-old, his wins normally come in early summer: May and July 2023, and June 2024. He has been dropped to only 78, and those wins were off 83, 86, and 83, so he should go close.
Shine On Brendan loves this course, being a multiple winner, and is upped in trip for this contest after keeping on over a mile last time out. He should be competitive here for a place at least.

This is one of the rank outsiders in the race but I don't see it that way at all. The horse is one of the least exposed in the race and a very good 3lb claiming Apprentice is booked. His only turf effort was on debut when placed in a maiden and there were quality horses all around him in that race. In fact, on that evidence it's easy to make a case for him having plenty in hand here and a return to turf could be the key after racing on the AW in the 6 runs since. The cheekpieces go on now and it looks like it could well be all systems go for this one now.

Not too many miles on the clock for the 4yo. Two runs last month for a new yard, 2nd of 11 last week over this 12f trip. One of the more likely runners who can take a step forward. He was rated 15lb higher at one point last summer.

6lb lower than when winning here last June, his fourth win at this track. His wins have come over a little shorter but he stays this far and acts on any ground so from a very tempting mark on the pick of his form, he could be worth taking a little chance on.

LADY PHOEBE finds a near-basement level handicap where she has course form effective on most ground type. She is third-up this spell with potential to peak and although a relatively long standing maiden this appears to be her best opportunity to date.
Sassy Glory ran well to finish 2nd in an apprentice handicap at Thirsk over 12f last September on similar going to that she will face at Hamilton. David Allan takes the ride.
Escaping the penalty for the last time out win will hugely benefit MESAAFI here. He looks the best of the bunch and is ahead of the handicapper, so is worth solid consideration.
Found an easy race to bounce back in. Good value at price and the horse has won me some good money in the past.

Gallant looks ready to bounce back after a luckless run at York, where he was hampered and never got a clear shot. He’s still lightly raced and returns to the all-weather, where he’s already a winner so should go well.
Has been fast improving lately. Trainer reaching his peak. Best closing figures and the trip looks ideal for this horse.

The 3-year-old was a good third on his handicap debut five weeks ago, a decent turf handicap but not helped with a poor passage. Interesting that he now reverts back to the AW. Only four career runs and plenty of room for improvement. Good apprentice booked for the ride and his 7lb claim should improve his chances.

Has 3 wins to his name all coming back to back to back last August to September all on the all weather 2 over this trip including over CD & the other at 9.5f . Has ran twice this season over 9.5 & 10f so drops back to 8f today & has place claims at decent price .

Keybaar made a very promising debut in a 6 furlongs Novice event at Kempton in April. There was substance to the form as the winner was beaten just a neck in a Windsor Novice under a penalty last month, and the 5th won at Southwell. With improvement likely, Keybaar looks the most likely winner.

I think we can forgive the last time out run at Brighton for LAZZAR, as it's not necessarily suitable for every horse. So maybe he fares better here, back in this sphere. He was generally running well up to that point.
Finished third on his last two starts at this track, both from a pound higher than this. Is not the easiest to win with but he is back on his last winning mark which came over C&D in December.

If Home and Dry finds some old form, it has the talent to win this. But clearly, it is a tough one to get ready. Its only win came back in 2021, but it has run well off higher marks than this and run to a 100 in recent hurdles races. It could be very well in here.

Won over course and distance by 22 lengths off a mark of 46 in November 2024. Just the 2 races since, and worth another look at this trip racing off 51 today. But with Rose Dawes' 5 pounds allowance, Certain Style is effectively racing off the same mark as that course and distance win.

The 3-year-old has been a little disappointing after earning an opening 80 handicap mark last year, now running off a 67 mark. However, he was a good 2nd of 11 four weeks ago, traveled strong, hit the front a furlong, and was unlucky to be headed late on. Something to build on, and these rivals don’t look great.
Previous course winner and well handicapped off 59 (won off 55). Has won at 6f and seems to excel at that distance. In form and well drawn.

Ruth Carr brings just one horse down from her Yorkshire stable, and Oisin Murphy takes the ride. Touchwood was a solid third last time out at Leicester and drops 1 lb for that effort. Solid chance here at Lingfield.

Things didn’t go to plan for the 4yo in his three runs this year - a little too keen. Not beaten far on his return run when tiring late on. The majority of his rivals that day were rated 76-79, now facing rivals rated 55-68. With the jockey’s claim he’s effectively a huge 17lb better off now. With a draw in stall 1 he could be given the freedom to front run.
A course and distance winner, she should appreciate the step up in trip after two races over 6 furlongs here this year, following a 4-month absence that she will strip fitter for.

Trained by Michael Appleby and ridden by 7lb claimer Mason Paetel, this five-year-old mare has demonstrated consistent form on the all-weather circuit. Notably, she secured a victory at Kempton on 28 May 2025 in a Class 6 handicap over 1 mile, showcasing her ability to handle different distances. Prior to that, she finished sixth at Chelmsford on 27 March 2025 in a Class 5 handicap over 7 furlongs, indicating her familiarity with the course. Her form figures suggest she has the ability to be competitive at this level.

The New Bay Pearl has been knocking on the door, placing in three of her last four starts on the all-weather. She was a solid third at Kempton over a mile last time, finishing strongly after being held up. Back to 7f today, which might suit better, and she’s got a decent shot if she gets a clear passage.

An open-looking handicap where the consistent Windsor Pass appeals at a big-looking 8/1. He has been right on the scene in most of his recent races off this mark, and with a good pace upfront assured, he can be produced late to land the spoils.

Maids Head looks poised to shed the Maiden tag here was last seen at Wolverhampton over the 6 furlong trip 30 days ago where finishing a respectable 4th/8 keeping of strongly inside the closing stages of that race and shaped in need of a step up in trip and that she has got here stepping up trip racing at the 7 furlong trip here at Chelmsford that being a good move by her connections as she can be shown to best effect over this trip and in my point of view she is very unlucky not have shed that Maiden tag already she is very consistent and a filly with plenty of potential and has already proved that statement as she has been placed a total of 6 times out of her 9 career starts and is more than capable of gaining a well deserved success here and i strongly believe this filly is capable of better than a mark 67 jockey R Havlin takes the ride on M Botti's inmate and can give Maids Head the perfect ride here at Chelmsford daughter of Pinatubo & Nashmiah ( Dam's sire Elusive City ) must be taken very seriously here . Respected .

5 times raced 3-year-old, signed off last season with a win at Thirsk on nursery handicap debut. Returned 5 weeks ago after 7 months off, unplaced, maybe needing the run. Winning jockey back on board has a good record at this track, as does the trainer.

PRINCESS PW has been a pretty consistent runner up to now and demonstrated plenty of ability here at the beginning of the year in a maiden. She seems to be at a workable handicap mark based on the runs up to now and could be a potential improver. There's a lot of hold-up sorts here, so she could get into a decent position from the stalls and stay there on this tight track.

Finished 6th of 11 at Newmarket in debut run in the U.K. for flats last month. But I think the yard will look for improvements. Sometimes, switching from turf to AW can be beneficial, and it is helped by dropping down 3 classes today.

Adelaide Bay is in cracking form, having won two of his last three starts, including a strong finish at Wolverhampton last time out. He’s up 3lb for that win but still looks well treated, especially from stall 2. With David Egan back on board and a return to Chelmsford, where he’s already a course and distance winner, he’s got a solid chance of going in again.
Should welcome the drop in trip after racing over 2 miles here 2 weeks ago, with further improvement possible on the second run following wind surgery.

Smokey Malone’s been flying lately and loves it round Chelmsford. He’s up a couple pounds for his last win here but still looks well in, especially with Hogan back on board. If he keeps up that form, he’s right in the mix again.

Enrolled is still chasing that first win but has been knocking on the door lately. He was a solid fourth at Goodwood last time, and the step up to 1m2f could be just what he needs. With Richard Kingscote in the saddle and a decent draw, he’s got a fair shout if he keeps progressing.

Raced twice over the all-weather, both over 1m. Finished 4l off the winner at Southwell and over 2l off the winner at Newcastle. Trainer in good all-weather form. The filly likes to be held up, which no horse should contest. This should allow her to get into a rhythm and pick off the others at the business end. Step up in trip is a positive.

Notimeforchitchat had a rough go over this course and distance last time, finishing well down the field. But he’s a two-time all-weather winner, including a tidy 7f success at Kempton in March. He’s still unexposed at this trip and gets Finley Marsh back on board. If he can bounce back to that earlier form, he’s got a decent shout in this field.

Still Coming Here is in good form (311) and was on a roll winning those 2 runs but halted with the switch from AW to turf and raised mark when 3 of 7 at Windsor last month. Given his ability, I am not surprised the mark remains unchanged, and it helps that he has course experience. Should welcome a return back to AW.

The model I run suggests Gavin should win this race. Gavin lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 7 runner field but looks well treated off an official ranking that's firmly middle order. This subsequently means Gavin goes out carrying nearly 1 stone less than the top weight and only 4 lbs more than the bottom weight. Gavin is a prior course and distance winner, so knows how to get the job done around this track. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Do It Like A Dude can win this one. Do It Like A Dude has the second highest RPR of this 5-horse lineup, and it looks like the main competition here should be Reina Del Mar. Do It Like A Dude carries the most initial weight in this race around this 2m 4f trip, but Callum Pritchard on board relieves 5 lbs of those, which is helpful. Do It Like A Dude is running for the second time post-wind operation and should have more to offer than the 3rd place finish when last out 29 days ago. Won his race before that, before a long break. If getting back to that form, Do It Like A Dude can offer much better value here than the short odds on favorite Reina Del Mar. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Looks to have a great chance, and I feel it should run a career best tomorrow. Form of last race looks strong for grade, and this looks like a slightly easier race. Usual jockey rides and big chance at fair odds.

The model I run suggests d'Jo Dela Barriere can win this one. This result has been driven by d'Jo Dela Barriere having a comparably high RPR to the rest of the 6 horse field and an official ranking leaving him well treated and carrying slightly less weight over this 2m 4f trip. Came a decent 3rd 14 days ago and looks to build on that finish here. Prior distance winner so knows how to get the nose in front over this trip. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Second last three times, beaten on the line, should make amends this time around. Jockey and trainer in good form. Would be a surprise if not in the first three.

The model I run suggests a win from Pooroldmackley is the value bet here. Pooroldmackley has shown some reasonable form lately but can't seem to get the head over the line first in the last couple of races. Lines up with a fairly middle order initial weight, but Ealonr Williams takes off a massive 7 lbs, which helps bring the total down to the second lowest of the runners around this 2m 7f trip. Form figures of 311-3 and looks to get back on top here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

A course and distance winner off a mark of 100 in April 2023 and is now down to a mark of 92. Runner-up behind Cloudy Wednesday when last seen 45 days ago and that horse has won again since to boost the form.

The model I run suggests McGregors Charge can win this one. This result has been driven by McGregors Charge having a comparably high RPR to the majority of the runners here in this 7-horse race, but an incredibly low official ranking relative to the other main competition. This leaves McGregors Charge carrying 1 stone less than the current market favorite and 1 stone and 10 lbs less than the top weight. Last ran 33 days ago after a break and looks to get back on track here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

The model I run suggests Pittsburg can win this one. This model result has been driven by Pittsburg having the highest RPR of the smaller 6 runner field, but lines up with a middle order official ranking. This results in Pittsburg carrying less weight than the current market favorite and top weight. Pittsburg has form figures of 53112 and is a prior winner at this distance. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Aidan O'Brien's two-year-olds are in excellent form, and expensive purchase Minerva looks likely to add to the impressive recent record with Ryan Moore riding.
Green Impact disappointed in the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket but went there without a run and probably needed the race. He looks the class horse in this Listed event.

Paddy Twomey (SR 18%) trained Currawood is chanced to beat Jessica Harrington trained favourite (and 2,000 Guineas sixth) Green Impact. The selection has been a steady improver in maiden company and ran out a comfortable five length winner at Cork in April. Second to the useful Officer at the Curragh a month ago at Listed level. That horse is a key formline (via Fields Of Gold and the Irish and English 2,000 Guineas). Currawood receives 5lbs from the likely favourite here and looks the better value of the two at current prices.

Value odds in this bet for Eastwatch, which only raced twice, being runner-up in debut and later winner, and is very lightly weighted. Though possible, it will not be easy to win in this company, but it is likely that the pick will make the frame.

At a massive price, I'm going to chance this J Nallen runner, Cristal Clere, which goes up in distance. With the trainer not coming here for nothing, normally with 3 from 6 wins, he must think something of it in this Listed contest. E/W.

It is probably sufficient to note that Ryan Moore has chosen to ride Acapulco Bay, of Aidan O'Brien's two colts, in this three-year-old Listed Event. He drops down in class from running in a Group 3 Derby Trial here last time.

A previous all-weather winner at Dundalk, Titanium Emperor arrives here making a second outing since making the switch from the AW. He showed enough promise last time out when he took an early lead before getting caught. But with that experience under his belt, I think he can go even better here and go close.
Bay Colony stepped up to win at Limerick. She has more on in this higher contest taking on males. Nice type with distance experience and has a place chance.

Pierre Royal should confirm the Gowran form with Daler from his first race when they were 2nd and 3rd to Aidan O'Brien's First Wave. Albeit, he is now on six pounds worse terms, having comfortably won at Gowran since over a mile in a second slower time than First Wave's win. So it was an improved run from Pierre Royal, and his mark of 88 seems generous.

Ran to form, beaten 7L in fifth in a race over 10f at Roscommon last time. Will probably come on for that run. Well in on the ratings and form, and now back to a more suitable distance IMO. Therefore, NAP today.

Ja'marr is possibly better on the all-weather at Dundalk but is still a capable performer. He could bounce back from underperforming last time at Cork when a beaten favorite in an apprentice handicap. Should get at least a place.

ECHINACEA is a likely improver up in trip with stamina on her dam side. That should serve her well ahead of her handicap debut today and the market appears to have overlooked this three year old filly taking on her own age group feasibly treated for this sphere of racing.

Great Mover was hampered in running at Fairyhouse last time over 7f where she lost ground and then ran on again towards the finish to be a close 3rd. She ran over a mile as a two year old so should not mind the extra furlong and should go close as the handicapper is due to raise her two pounds.

Alan McIntyre’s MOONHALL LASS has a pop at a mile today. Based on her performance LTO in Roscommon, keeping on well inside the dying stages, suggests to my untrained eye she might need that extra furlong. Adding to that, that’s 2 x 0-90s she’s run well in now, boxing above her division 65 rated. This drop to the 0-70 grade with the handicapper shaving off another 2lb could be what the doctor ordered. If they punted this filly 16/1-11/2f LTO in that grade, they’ll surely fancy this today, if she stays the mile of course.

I wasn’t planning to get involved in this contest, but a good friend & fellow tipster had me take a second look - and from a price perspective alone, WIDELY ACCLAIMED looks far too tempting to ignore at current odds of 20/1. This 3-year-old colt, trained by Ado McGuinness, was only a length behind MOONHALL LASS - today’s shorter-priced rival - just 24 days ago at Roscommon (7½f, Good), where the latter was backed into favouritism.
A Son of ACLAIM, WIDELY ACCLAIMED finished a staying-on 5th that day and now drops 3lbs in the weights, which could prove key. He steps up slightly in trip here, and that move looks a positive on the back of his closing effort last time out.
McGuinness might have only the one recent winner, but he boasts an impressive 38.89% strike rate for runners hitting the frame in the past fortnight. Retained rider Adam Caffrey - who knows this horse well - has a solid 30.77% place strike rate for the yard over the past year.
Given the form lines, weight drop, and encouraging trainer/jockey stats, I’d be kicking myself if I didn’t have at least a small play at these odds.
Johnny Murtagh sticks on the cheekpiece here on Amber Blossom, which may have a positive effect. It's on a good mark for this and looks a lively outsider.

Three runs for a mark on the AW but did much better on handicap and turf debut at Roscommon last time out. That was from a 3lb higher mark over half a furlong shorter. She did the best of her work late on there, so the longer trip is going to suit her well.

MICASSO is a three year old who has been catching the eye in behind those placed in recent oiutings. He should benefit from this step up to a mile handicapping and he is well drawn for early track position taking in this left-hand turn. Dangerous at rewarding odds if he gets a run as second reserve overnight.

Dark Viper finally lost his maiden tag on his penultimate race, having finished 2nd seven times last season and also first time out this season. Not so good last time, 3rd of 6 having been put up 5 pounds, but he is now dropped two pounds back and should still be competitive.

First run for new stable. Very interesting off lower rating, gelded, middle of 2024. 86 now, was at height when won 93. Stable in good form. Ground probably too testing when beaten over 7L at Doncaster last time each way.

Trained by Adrian McGuinness and ridden by apprentice J A Powell, this six-year-old gelding has demonstrated consistent form that suggests he could be competitive here. Notably, he secured a victory at Dundalk on 12 January 2025 in a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs, showcasing his potential when conditions suit. In his most recent outing on 25 May 2025 at the Curragh, Exquisite Acclaim finished tenth in a Class 4 handicap over 7 furlongs, beaten by 6 lengths. Prior to that, he was unplaced at Naas on 5 May 2025 over the same distance, indicating a need to recapture his earlier form. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level. 
The return to Leopardstown's turf surface, where he has previously performed well, could play to his strengths. With J A Powell's 7lb claim, he receives a weight advantage that may enhance his competitiveness. 
Given his recent performances and the race conditions, Exquisite Acclaim presents as a viable each-way option for those seeking value in this contest.

Trainer Gerard O'Leary (SR 17%) had a close second at 25-1 in a Premier Handicap yesterday. The market is keen on Zipster. The 4yo by Zoustar has been getting closer with each run, pretty much, in four starts for this trainer (formerly UK-based with the Crisfords; won two races for them at a mile. Those wins off marks of 69 and 70.) Dropped 2 lbs today down to OR71 despite a good run over a trip further than this two weeks ago. This is an open race but Zipster looks on the verge of scoring his first win for in-form yard. Good draw in stall 5. Shane Foley rides.

Kaptain Bay has been performing well over hurdles with a 2nd place and a win in his last two races. He returns to the flat off a decent mark of 71 over a shorter distance than the 12f he ran his last two flat races over.

Unterberg is still a maiden after 13 starts on turf, but he has twice finished second in Cork handicaps. The first time was over 9 furlongs last August, and he repeated that when beaten by 1 length there last month. He is off the same mark here and must have a good each-way chance with 5 places on offer.

Loingseoir has been hanging out in the mid division and back, but running on. So if it does that today here on this track, I don't think it will do anything. It has a plum draw in 6 under the same pilot, N Burns, after dropping a pound or two. It has a big chance today.

WHIST comes from a shrewd smart yard who can get one ready following a break. This owner/bred filly will likely not have shown her full hand through qualifying and she appears to be starting out life in the handicap sphere from an atractive looking opening mark. Maybe the yard will be looking to capitalise by landing some bets today.

Trained by Andrew Slattery and ridden by Andrew Joseph Slattery, this four-year-old gelding has demonstrated consistent form that suggests he could be competitive here. In his most recent outing on 18 May 2025 at Naas, Killeaney Bear finished second in a handicap over 1 mile, beaten by 3¾ lengths. Prior to that, he was second at Cork on 10 May 2025 in a maiden hurdle over 2 miles and 1 furlong, indicating his versatility across different race types. Notably, he secured a victory at Leopardstown on 8 August 2024 in a handicap over 1 mile and 1 furlong, showcasing his potential when conditions suit. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level. 
The return to Leopardstown's turf surface, where he has previously performed well, could play to his strengths. With the experience gained from his recent runs and a return to a course he favors, he could be poised to deliver a strong performance.

Eastern Wind is up in class and down in distance here but could still go close off bottom weight. She has won her last two races which were a 12f handicap at Bellewstown followed by a maiden hurdle at Tipperary.
